# ab-test-playbook

> An A/B testing and CRO engine that runs inside Claude Code. It suggests experiment scenarios from a curated archive of 221 (e-commerce, mobile app, SaaS/B2B, and regulated finance, insurance and private-pension flows), designs new single-variable tests for a page you share, audits an existing test plan for methodological, UX and ethics flaws, and renders every scenario as a self-contained 16:9 HTML card that shows only the comparison: the test's question, Variant A and B side by side, the changed element ringed and named. Each proposal is a short structured record (title, problem, one-sentence mechanism, variable, A/B difference, primary KPI with its denominator, guardrail, source and evidence, priority, and a warning only when needed), kept in its JSON (the card prints only its title, chat only a one-line tag), at most three strong ones per turn by default; the archive keeps its three-box format, and a proposal gets the three boxes only when the user asks for detail. It doesn't analyze results or compute sample size, duration, significance or a winner; the user's testing tool reports those. Open source, MIT, stdlib-only.

The playbook is opinionated on purpose. Five rules it will not bend: one variable per variant pair; exactly one primary KPI plus at least one guardrail that measures an independent harm (an accessibility guardrail is a pass/fail check with a criterion); no dark patterns and no treating security or consent steps as removable friction; every proposal states its evidence level (your own data, an archive pattern, a sector observation, or intuition; an archive pattern is a curated idea, never presented as tested); and no sample-size, duration or significance claims at all.

Delivery is gated: the validator and the card builder refuse what code can check (a difference outside the ring, a changed number, an interactive addition without accessibility criteria, a revenue primary that could hide user harm, personal-data values), two review agents check what code can't, and the final card builds only when both reviews' fingerprint stamps match the content.

Install in Claude Code with `/plugin marketplace add ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook` followed by `/plugin install ab-test-playbook@ab-test-playbook`. Needs `python3` 3.9 or newer; the scripts use the standard library only. A skills-only install through the skills CLI is limited: it omits the rules, archive and scripts.

## Core documentation

- [README](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/README.md): what it does, install, usage, and a worked session from screenshot to card
- [Binding rules (CLAUDE.md)](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): the 19 non-negotiable rules every skill obeys
- [Architecture](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): where judgement lives versus where enforcement lives, and why review is split across two agents
- [FAQ](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/FAQ.md): common questions about scope, guardrails, priority and usage
- [Methodology](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/knowledge/methodology.md): experiment design, KPI and guardrail rules, variable isolation, priority tiers and fit

## Questions it answers

- What A/B tests should I run on an e-commerce checkout, cart, or product detail page?
- How do I write an A/B test hypothesis that states a mechanism rather than a guess?
- Which metrics belong in a test as guardrails, and why is one primary KPI mandatory?
- Is my variant a dark pattern, or does it change a regulated display?
- What mistakes invalidate an A/B test result before it even starts?
- How do I prioritise which CRO experiments to run first?
- Is my existing test plan set up correctly, or does it have a confound?
- What can I test inside an insurance, pension or credit flow without touching regulated copy?

## Reference

- [Scenario schema](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/blob/main/templates/scenario.schema.json): the compact scenario record, a platform-agnostic test definition portable to any experimentation tool
- [Scenario archive](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/tree/main/knowledge/scenarios): 221 curated scenarios grouped by journey stage, in 13 files, including finance, insurance and private pension
- [Examples](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/tree/main/examples): sample scenario records carried end to end, definition through rendered card, plus an audit of a flawed test proposal
- [Sample cards](https://github.com/ali-demirbas/ab-test-playbook/tree/main/docs/demo): the rendered sample cards on different screen types
- [Live card demo](https://ali-demirbas.github.io/ab-test-playbook/): the real output of the card builder, no install
